formula: examples x impact x confidence / effort

items.title: Path traversal and symlink escapes through values that do not come from a web request
items.summary: Misses where the attacker-controlled value arrives through a workflow context, a parsed document attribute or a library parameter rather than req.query, so no source is modelled; plus walks and archives that never check for symlinks. Source and sink catalogues exist; the gap is source modelling and cross-file propagation.
items.reproducer: values from a workflow context, a missing symlink check and a parsed XSD attribute
items.effortReason: cross-file symbol resolution plus a handful of new source kinds

items.title: Code, command and argument injection through forwarded keyword arguments and generated code
items.summary: Library entry points that forward **kwargs to a CLI or interpolate a parsed value into generated source. The taint engine tracks a value to a call but not through argument forwarding and code-generation templates.
items.reproducer: keyword arguments forwarded to git commands and a code-generator template
items.effortReason: summary keys that carry keyword-argument maps, bounded by E2-05's budgets

items.title: Independent entries whose vulnerable file is not in the materialised scope
items.summary: Entries the root-cause record labels as corpus-scoping issues: they are scored as misses although the vulnerable code was deleted by the fix or lives outside the packaged scope. (The record's prose says five; four table rows carry the label, and that count is what is scored here.) That penalises the engine for the dataset; it must be separated from engine gaps before any rate is quoted.
items.reproducer: the root-cause record explains each entry
items.effortReason: label the entries unscored in the manifest with the reason

items.title: Authorization and ownership checks the engine cannot see (IDOR, missing auth, cross-workspace)
items.summary: The largest cluster of independent misses where the fix adds an ownership, workspace or permission check that the engine never modelled as missing: handlers that forward query or body identifiers to a service with no scope check, sibling routes that carry middleware while one does not, and checks ANDed in the wrong way. These need route-to-service-to-persistence comparison, which DCI is built for, not another pattern.
items.reproducer: each entry's evidence column cites the missing check
items.effortReason: needs cross-route and cross-layer propagation (E4-03) and measured families (E4-06)

items.title: SSRF where the guard lives in a different file or the redirect is followed
items.summary: Client-controlled URLs reaching an HTTP client across files, and outbound clients that follow a redirect into internal space. Some sinks are covered by accident; the guard model (what counts as a validated fetch) is not.
items.effortReason: cross-file resolution of the guarded-fetch helper plus redirect handling in the sink model
items.trace: the record traces these misses to an HTTP client with no guard on the path from a client-controlled URL (GHSA-gcvv, GHSA-g366), a redirect followed without re-validation (GHSA-c9hr) and a sink matched only by accident (GHSA-rfr2)

items.title: Sensitive data returned before the authorization decision is computed
items.summary: Responses that spread a full model into the body before a permission flag is evaluated, and cross-tenant namespace queries without segment anchoring. These are ordering and scoping properties of a handler, so they belong with the invariant work.
items.hypothesis: the pattern is write-after-read ordering inside one handler (response built before the access decision); an invariant of the form 'authorization checked before the response is assembled' would catch it. Not yet reproduced against the current engine.

items.title: Third-party repository completion was 3 of 10 and its causes were not separated
items.summary: A scored run completed 3 of 10 targets. Without separating clone, tool, parser, timeout and engine causes the number cannot say whether the engine or the setup failed.
items.reproducer: docs/SCORECARD.md line 417: 3/10 targets completed at the recorded bundle
items.effortReason: reproduce per target, classify, fix the engine-controlled categories

items.title: Five documents state 17 MCP tools; the server registers 23
items.summary: Found by the E0-01 inventory. Documentation drift is not a detection problem, but it is a public claim that is wrong at HEAD.

items.title: Findings produced and then lost (suppression, sanitizer assumptions, CWE remapping)
items.summary: One independent miss was a detector that silently discarded every finding it produced. Others show a finding present under a different file or CWE. A stage-by-stage candidate ledger is the way to find the rest instead of guessing.
items.reproducer: scanner/src/sast/rate-limit.js discarded all findings because they carried no `vuln` field (fixed in 640da42); the root-cause record documents it
items.effortReason: instrument the lifecycle once, then triage what the ledger shows

items.title: Java parser lowers this.method(...) to the literal "unknown"
items.summary: Recorded as flagged and not started in the SARD ledger: calls through `this` do not resolve in the Java call graph, hiding intra-class flows.
items.trace: the SARD ledger records that parser-java lowers `this.method(...)` to the literal "unknown", so the call never enters the call graph (section "What remains genuinely open")

items.title: No independent measurement exists for the current engine
items.summary: The published scorecard describes the current engine with only a curated regression net; the only independent figures are for engine 0.141.0 with a dirty measurement worktree. Every accuracy statement about the current engine is unsupported until a clean-commit run exists.
items.reproducer: docs/SCORECARD.md states 'no independent evaluation of this engine' and bench/independent/gate-baseline.json records engine 0.141.0
items.effortReason: hours of network fetch and scanning, run in checkpointed shards

items.title: C# taint propagation gap for LDAP, XPath and command-injection source shapes
items.summary: Five plausible mechanisms were tested and ruled out in the SARD ledger; the cause is unidentified. The PRD names C# input-source propagation as a confirmed historical gap to re-check in the current checkout.
items.hypothesis: a source shape shared by the three CWE families is not propagated; needs a probe on synthetic twins, not corpus access
items.effortReason: probe, then a targeted propagation fix with safe sibling

items.title: Incremental cache keys may miss transitive dependency and feed-freshness changes
items.summary: The incremental cache is keyed by content and tool version. Changing a callee or a sanitizer in another file, or advancing the advisory feed, must invalidate dependents; a stale clean result is a false green.
items.hypothesis: scanner/src/dataflow/incremental.js and k2-summary-cache.js invalidate on file content; transitive callers and feed age are the unproven part. E6-04 builds the counterexample test.

items.title: Analyzer isolation does not cap memory or CPU per worker
items.summary: The supervisor isolates analyzer failures and timeouts; no RSS or CPU limit is enforced per worker, so a runaway analyzer can exhaust the host before the timeout fires.
items.hypothesis: scanner/src/pipeline/analyzer-supervisor.js bounds time and restarts workers; no resource limit is passed to the worker. E6-05 reproduces with an allocation loop.
items.effortReason: supervised workers with limits on the existing supervisor

items.title: Several patch routes may not share one verification contract
items.summary: CLI fix, MCP apply_fix, autopilot and SCA upgrades exist, and a hypothesis-level verification record exists in the assurance contracts. Whether every route produces the same patch-level verdict, and whether a deny-all patch is rejected everywhere, is not established.
items.hypothesis: the routes were built at different times (fix-verify-loop, apply-fix-service, deterministic-fix) and each may apply a different subset of checks; E3-01 produces the contract table that confirms or refutes this
items.effortReason: one verifier behind every route, with compatibility adapters
